newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew to delay repair work on module.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew to delay repair work on module.

text.p: The crew of the Mir space station need more time than originally expected to prepare to enter the punctured Spektr module for repair works, flight director Vladimir Solovyov said on Friday.

"This is a rather complicated job...and that is why the sortie into Spektr is put off to July 17 or 18," he told reporters. Two Russian cosmonauts had been expected to try to reconnect Spektr's solar panels to the main batteries on July 11 or 14 following a docking accident last week.

Solovyov also said he hoped the latest problem to hit Mir -- the malfunctioning of special devices which keep Mir's solar panels facing the sun to soak up maximum power for the energy-starved craft -- would be fixed by Saturday.

"We expect that by the time Progress is launched we will be able to cope with the gyrodines' problem," Solovyov said in a reference to the launch of the Progress cargo ship which is planned for Saturday morning to deliver relief equipment to Mir.
Earlier on Friday, Interfax news agency quoted Mission Control as saying it had worked out why the devices had failed and the crew would be able to fix the problem later in the day.

But Solovyov was more cautious. "We are about to find the reason (of the failure), but at this very moment it has not been found," he said, adding the problem would not affect the docking between Mir and Progress.
